properties.name: Graph theory undergirds reflow2 — the design's shape is analysed with real algorithms, owned in-tree, not obtained
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-17, thinking out loud about the subsystem decomposition — his words, and they had never been written as a requirement until 2026-08-24:

> *"I wanted graph theory to undergird everything (that's why I designed reflow2 to use dynograph-foundation). graph theory was important to my concept of reflow2."*

⭐ **WHY IT WAS WRITTEN THEN, AND NOT BEFORE.** Until 2026-08-24 this need was expressed structurally rather than as intent: five Interfaces at `designation: required`, of which `ifc:req-dyno-graph-api` said *reflow2 NEEDS graph algorithms from outside*. **A required interface is a legitimate way to have no requirement** — the design was not claiming to DO the thing, it was claiming to NEED it, and the supplier's own design carried the why.

Absorbing the algorithms deletes that framing. Once `leiden`, `cut_structure`, `strongly_connected_components` and the rest sit in `cmp:graph-algorithms`, nothing in the design says why reflow2 detects communities at all, and `unmotivated_capability` would be right to fire. `dec:absorbed-code-is-distributed-by-function` made writing this a CONDITION of increments 3-5 rather than cleanup after them, precisely so the gap never opens.

═══ WHAT THIS REQUIRES ═══

That reflow2 reads a design's SHAPE, not only its text — that structural facts a reader cannot see by reading nodes one at a time are computed and reported. Concretely, what the shape is asked today: are there cycles in the dependency spine; which parts form communities that barely talk to each other; which single parts, if removed, disconnect the rest; which nodes are unreachable from the thread; which parts sit on the most paths between others.

And that the algorithms doing it are OWNED, not obtained. A design brain whose central analysis is borrowed can have that analysis withdrawn, versioned away, or changed under it — and reflow2's whole claim is that it can say what it knows and why.

═══ 🛑 WHAT THIS IS NOT, so it is not read wider than it is ═══

• NOT a requirement for graph algorithms in general. Nine files were deliberately left upstream — pagerank, eigenvector, closeness, clustering, link prediction, max-flow, shortest path, toposort, degree centrality — because nothing in reflow2 asks those questions. **Owning what you use is the requirement; owning a library is not.**
• NOT a claim that the current set is complete. It is what the detectors ask today.
• NOT a performance or scale requirement. The absorbed implementations are EXACT rather than approximate on the stated ground that design graphs are 10^2-10^3 nodes; if a design ever outgrows that, this requirement does not say what should happen.

═══ DISTINCT FROM ITS NEAR NEIGHBOURS ═══

`dec:absorbed-code-is-distributed-by-function` decides WHERE absorbed code lives and made this capture a condition; it does not say why reflow2 wants graph theory. `req:coherence` ("design stays coherent across its lifecycle") is the OUTCOME the detectors serve — this is about the analysis underneath them being real and owned, and a design could satisfy coherence with no graph theory at all. `dec:idea-is-the-foundation-a-subsystem-or-a-supplier` quotes the same sentence but asks where the system boundary sits.

═══ ✅ ACCEPTED BY ANTHONY, 2026-08-24 — and the route here is worth keeping ═══

It was captured at `proposed` and moved to `accepted` on his explicit word ("accept the proposed requirement"), with his approver edge, minutes apart.

**The two-step was not ceremony.** He stated this as MOTIVATION inside a brainstorm about subsystem placement a week earlier, not as intent — and promoting a musing to an accepted requirement on his behalf is the forgery `dec:certainty-derived` forbids. The distance between "he said it" and "he meant it as a requirement" is exactly what the `proposed` status exists to hold, and it cost one question to close honestly.

⭐ IT ALSO SAT UNWRITTEN FOR A WEEK. The sentence was in the graph the whole time, inside a brainstorm node, doing nothing. What surfaced it was not a search but a CONSEQUENCE: absorbing the code removed the structure that had been standing in for the requirement. **Intent stated as motivation is invisible to every detector until something makes its absence load-bearing.**
